title: Army to detonate US stockpile of bomb-making chemicals in Iowa the day before Thanksgiving
summary: The U.S. Army says it plans to detonate the nation's entire stockpile of lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday morning. It says waiting any longer raises the risks that the dangerously degrading bomb-making chemicals could explode at any time. Officials sought to assure residents that they’ve taken steps to put barriers around the blast zone and limit the plume from the detonation when it happens the day before Thanksgiving. Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle said Tuesday there's no reason to panic. The controlled detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown has set off concerns about potential health and environmental effects and frustration over a lack of information.

title: US Army to detonate degraded bomb-making material in Iowa after getting court approval
summary: The U.S. Army plans to detonate bomb-making chemicals in Iowa on Wednesday morning after getting approval from a federal appeals court in a saga that has sowed confusion and included an unusual twist from President Donald Trump. In a statement late Monday, the Army said it’s proceeding with a controlled removal of 68 barrels of lead azide in coordination with state, local and federal authorities. A three-judge panel of the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals said earlier Monday that the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency adequately incorporated safeguards in an emergency permit to minimize the dispersal of dust.

title: Democratic Rep. Jimmy Gomez resigns after Ethics panel finds evidence of sexual misconduct
summary: Democratic Rep. Jimmy Gomez of California is resigning from Congress after the House Ethics Committee released a report finding “substantial evidence” he engaged in sexual misconduct toward a staffer. The committee said in a report Monday that Gomez's unwelcome sexual advances and sexual contact caused the aide significant and ongoing distress and contributed to her decision to leave House employment. Gomez said he has “strong disagreements" with the Ethics panel's findings but announced he will resign from Congress on Dec. 1. Gomez was already set to depart Congress at the end of the year, having been defeated in his bid for reelection this month by a fellow Democrat.
